newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Quebrada Blanca miners to return to work.
newsitem.headline: Chile Quebrada Blanca miners to return to work.

text.p: Striking Chilean Quebrada Blanca copper miners have accepted the company's pay offer after all-night talks and will start work from the evening shift Friday, said the mine's general manager, James Drake.
"They signed the offer at 4 a.m. this morning and the buses will be leaving for the mine at 11 a.m.," Drake told Reuters.
Drake said union leaders accepted the company's final pay offer of 15 percent increase in real terms over the next three years.
"The offer is respectable and keeps Quebrada Blanca in the Chilean market place in terms of wages," he said.
The union had no comment on the talks.
Drake said the mine was able to operate at 50 percent of design capacity during the nine-day walkout by using contractors and non-striking staff.
The pit, which lies on a remote plateau near the Bolivian border, produces 75,000 tonnes of copper cathodes a year.
Quebrada Blanca is controlled by Vancouver-based Cominco Ltd, Cominco Resources and Teck Resources International. ((-- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595x212))
